channel.title: Chokepoint
channel.description: AI chokepoint companies, numbers from filings

item.title: WuXi AppTec Comes Off the US 1260H List, and the Label Is Shrinking
item.description: Being on the list meant one more review for drugmakers doing business in the US. Removal lowers that cost, but whether orders changed is a question for the annual report.

item.title: Water at 45℃ is enough to go chiller-free, but 67% green power is the hard part to copy
item.description: This campus costs one-fifth as much to build as a US data center, the key saving is dropping the central chiller, and the hardest part to copy is where the power comes from.

item.title: Texas Calls a Halt to Data Centers, and GE Vernova's 18 GW Reservations May Loosen First
item.description: A governor-elect's one sentence already had the Nasdaq down 1% in pre-market trading, and it bears on whether AI data centers can be built on schedule.

item.title: Central bank draws a line: keep stocks, bonds and currency stable, and prevent systemic financial risk
item.description: This statement comes from a high level and draws wide attention, but it only sets a floor and does not say which way things will go, so ordinary people should not treat it as a buy or sell signal.

item.title: Pay-as-you-go API at a dozen-odd yuan a day far exceeds GPT Plus and Claude Pro in one month
item.description: Many people think pay-as-you-go is cheap and that topping up is no burden. In fact, the money often disappears quietly during long conversations.

item.title: Volume rose at 10:50, prices held in the afternoon, but the bond market has not passed the test yet.
item.description: When bonds are sold under pressure, a short pause in prices does not mean the danger is over, so watch the cost of borrowing to see the real picture.

item.title: Revenue rose 32.9%, but operating profit fell $10.9M
item.description: Sales keep rising, but the money earned keeps falling, which shows growth has not yet turned into profit, and anyone watching $KTOS should pay attention to this.

item.title: Kratos burned $18.9 million in the second quarter. The $9.3 million from selling Valkyrie made the number look smaller.
item.description: The burn figure was pulled down by income from selling an asset. To see the real pace of cash use, take that money out first.

item.title: Wild Halloween Costumes Do Not Mean People Are Out of Control
item.description: Costumes on the street may look shocking, but most people are just playing a role for the holiday, so do not guess about their private lives from what they wear.

item.title: AeroVironment Wins $43 million Antenna Order, Only 2.0% of Guidance Midpoint
item.description: The sum is not large, but it is part of the second-half ramp that is already booked, which is far more solid than deals still under negotiation.

item.title: $AVAV Revenue Fell 25.1% Quarter on Quarter, and Its $2.175 billion Guidance Depends on Orders Recovering
item.description: Revenue fell this fast, yet the company still guided to $2.175 billion, and whether that target can be met depends on orders returning to their earlier high.

item.title: In my pinned post on October 24, I wrote: the thinnest evidence right now is in power.
item.description: Two companies reported third-quarter results this week, and after rereading their filings, I need to change my earlier view that power has the thinnest evidence.

item.title: One Image, 3D Object in 3 Seconds: Idol Is Open Source and Runs on 7.2 GB of VRAM
item.description: Making a 3D model used to take professional software skills and a high-end graphics card. Now you drop in one image, and an ordinary computer may be able to run it. The barrier is much lower.

item.title: A new model quietly joined Arena. Does its tone match? Don't judge it from one or two rounds.
item.description: The codename does not show which company made the model, and Arena is a blind test, so judging its style depends on what you ask it.

item.title: Oppenheimer Sets First $205 Price Target on AeroVironment, About 74% Above Close
item.description: In the same month, brokers set $AVAV price targets anywhere from $165 to $237, a gap wide enough to take a closer look.

item.title: Don't Only Watch the Total Margin Balance. Tomorrow, Watch Net Financing Repayment.
item.description: The total amount borrowed to trade stocks can be misleading, while repayment activity shows whether anyone is being forced to sell.

item.title: Serenity (@aleabitoreddit) Reposts a Citi Line: Lasers and Optical Fiber Are Being Treated as the Next HBM
item.description: I went through the latest quarterly reports of the four laser companies Serenity mentions most, and revenue is surging at all four, but one company's books made me pause.

item.title: Anthropic model token volume on OpenRouter rose 3.6x after Opus 5.5 launched
item.description: This number shows that people are using it, but it comes from only one platform. It cannot be taken as direct evidence of Anthropic's total usage or reputation.

item.title: Micron's last quarter revenue was $54.23B, more than TSMC's $46.72B
item.description: Micron's gross margin was 86.8%, 20 points above TSMC, and I checked four upstream companies' quarterly reports since late September to see where AI spending is landing, using only figures the companies disclosed themselves.

item.title: Meta's Five-Year Default Insurance Price Hits a Record High, Latest at 114.5 bps
item.description: The price of this insurance has hit a record, which shows the market is more worried than ever about whether a big company can pay back its debt.

item.title: AeroVironment's LOCUST laser weapon wins its first overseas commercial order, worth $52 million
item.description: A foreign buyer has placed an order for a laser weapon for the first time. This shows that this type of equipment is moving toward commercial sale, not just staying in development.

item.title: One Prompt From Jensen Lets the Agent Set Itself Up
item.description: Setting up an AI assistant used to mean configuring it step by step by hand. This demo shows that the setup can be handed to AI, which is a signal for people who want to start using agents.

item.title: Compute can go live as soon as 14 days after the data center is built
item.description: Nvidia pre-builds and tests DSX POD before delivery, so AI builders can start using compute faster.

item.title: Mistral and NVIDIA Team Up to Bring AI Into Industrial Engineering Design Rooms
item.description: Engineers spend a lot of time on simulation and chip design. This partnership aims to have AI help directly, which affects the people who actually build things.

item.title: DeepSeek Processes 155 trillion tokens a Day and Earns $38 per GPU Hour
item.description: Until now, outsiders could mostly only guess whether AI services make money. DeepSeek has published its own revenue figures, so anyone can run the numbers with real data.

item.title: DeepSeek Orders 160,000 Huawei Ascend 950DT, but Delivery Could Take More Than a Year
item.description: The order is not the problem. Capacity for high-end memory and similar parts is the bottleneck, so this large order can only be delivered slowly.

item.title: $AVAV signs three MOUs in one week, but the press release has no amounts, and the stock fell about 5% on October 14
item.description: A cooperation memorandum sounds exciting, but it has no amount and no binding force, so it is still far from a real order.

item.title: $KTOS Announced Awards "More Than $100 Million," but No Matching Filing Shows Up
item.description: A number only counts toward expectations once it can be matched to official filings. Otherwise, it is just news.

item.title: $KTOS Gains One More Analyst, but Average Price Target Falls from $99.57 to $98.33
item.description: An analyst's price target shows their view of the stock, and this time more analysts issued one while the average target went down, so it is worth a closer look.
